original_question: Mutations in which gene cause the form of lactate dehydrogenase deficiency also known as glycogen storage disease type XI?

final_qi.question: Mutations in which gene cause the form of lactate dehydrogenase deficiency also known as glycogen storage disease type XI?
final_qi.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type XI corresponds to lactate dehydrogenase-A (LDH-A) deficiency. This disorder is produced by loss-of-function mutations in the LDHA gene, which encodes the muscle (A) subunit of lactate dehydrogenase needed for anaerobic glycolysis in skeletal muscle.

0.question: What is glycogen storage disease type XI?

final_answer.long_answer: Glycogen storage disease type XI (lactate dehydrogenase deficiency) is caused by pathogenic mutations in the LDHA gene, which encodes the A (muscle) subunit of the enzyme lactate dehydrogenase. Loss-of-function variants impair conversion of pyruvate to lactate in glycolysis, leading to the characteristic myopathic symptoms and exercise-induced myoglobinuria that define this form of GSD.
